questions.q: In a genuinely multi-cloud org, what role should Entra ID play relative to AWS and any other cloud?
options: Entra ID should sync a separate copy of identity into each cloud, and each cloud keeps its own source of truth
The single identity source of truth, with every cloud federating into it as a relying party
Entra ID should only govern Microsoft 365, with AWS and other clouds handled entirely independently
Each cloud should run its own identity provider and periodically reconcile with Entra ID
questions.explain: The pattern that scales is one source of truth — Entra ID owns who exists and what they're allowed — with every cloud, including AWS, consuming that decision as a relying party rather than maintaining its own authority.

questions.q: What is the difference between IdP-initiated and SP-initiated SAML sign-in to AWS?
options: IdP-initiated requires a password; SP-initiated does not
SP-initiated only works for admin users
IdP-initiated means the user starts from Entra ID's app portal and gets sent to AWS; SP-initiated means the user starts at the AWS access portal URL and gets redirected to Entra ID first
There is no real difference; both terms describe the identical flow
questions.explain: IdP-initiated sign-in starts at the identity provider (Entra ID's My Apps portal); SP-initiated sign-in starts at the service provider (the AWS access portal URL), which then redirects to Entra ID to authenticate before bouncing the user back.

questions.q: How does an Entra ID group like aws-prod-readonly actually grant access in AWS once federation is set up?
options: It is mapped to an AWS permission set, so group membership in Entra ID determines which IAM policies the user effectively has in the target AWS accounts
The group name itself is parsed by AWS as a literal IAM policy document
It has no effect in AWS; permission sets must always be assigned per individual user
It only works if the user also has a standalone AWS IAM access key
questions.explain: Entra ID groups are mapped to AWS IAM Identity Center permission sets, so adding or removing someone from the group changes their effective AWS access without any manual AWS console step.

questions.q: Why does federated access through AWS STS improve on long-lived IAM access keys?
options: STS credentials cost less than access keys
STS credentials are short-lived and tied to a recent, validated sign-in, instead of being a standing secret that can be leaked and used indefinitely
STS credentials never expire, unlike access keys
STS is only used for AWS billing, not authentication
questions.explain: After a SAML assertion is validated, IAM Identity Center issues short-lived, auto-expiring STS credentials — there's no standing secret sitting around waiting to be leaked, unlike a long-lived IAM access key.

questions.q: As an organization adds more AWS accounts, why is it risky to let a team create a local IAM user instead of using federation?
options: Local IAM users are always more expensive than federated access
AWS technically blocks the creation of local IAM users once federation is enabled
Local IAM users automatically inherit federation permissions, making the exception pointless
Every such exception recreates the three-directory problem — a group change in Entra ID will no longer control that account's access
questions.explain: Each local IAM user created as a shortcut is a thread back to separate, un-synced identity — it won't be affected when the equivalent Entra ID group changes, reintroducing exactly the inconsistency federation was meant to remove.
